entries.german:
Nicolaus schreibt dern Rudolf Losse, - boten des erzbischofs Saldewin von Trier am pdbstlichen Jtofe, iiber die feMe des erzbiscliofs mit Erfurt, iiber den hrieg zwischen kaiser Ludwig und kbnig Iohann von Sbhmen, iiber die Iudenverfolgung und andere ereignisse. (Trier) 1336 sept. 23.

Pater et domine mi graciosissime. Regracior vobis de multis beneficiis michi per vos impensis et adhuc ut spero sine dubio impendendis. Noveritis, quod literas vestras Her. fratri vestro de Pordicz et adhuc uno inissas per vos statim per Wig. nuncium domini Treverensis ulterius Ysen. procuravi, sicut eciam vobis nuper scripsi. Et credo vos habere responsum super dictis literis, quia noviter vobis misimus dominus meus et ego tres literas dictorum Hermanni fratris vestri etc. Item literam vestram plebano Bacheraoensi per vos missam hodie magister Wicker sibi portat, qui vadis supra Renum. Item scharsam vestram Lud. cellarius domini mei vobis reservavit. Item plantas et ignicorium ego vobis reservabo, sicut eciam vobis noviter scripsi. Item presentavit mihi unus clericus unain peccam, quam aperui et inveni unum librum scriptuin, duos libros papir. non scriptos et unum cingulum, sicut michi in litera vestra scripsistis, quod totum vobis reservam. Item presentavit michi . idem clericus duos libros eodem die, quas statim sequenti die misi fratri vestro Ysen. cum Io. scol. magistri Eck. notarii civium Erfordensium. Item rogo et consulo, quatenus vobis ordinetis et procuretis diversas res in curia, quia invenietur* ibi in meliori foro, quam alibi, et michi mittatis vobis reservandum. Item unum nuncium non mittatis vacumn ire ad partes de curia, nisi sibi aliquid detis ad portandum de rebus vestris. Item misi vobis tribus vicibus literas meas; nescio enim utrum vobis presentate sunt vel non, quia vos nichil michi scribitis de ipsis. — Item domina marchionissa antiqua ordinavit et fecit compo- sitionem inter dominum Treverensem, marchionem Mysnensem et Erfordenses. Qui Erfor- dienses dabunt domino Treverenst et . . marchioni in toto pro omnibus expensis, dampnis et pro compositioiie decem milia marcarum argenti preter dampna, que fecerunt domino Treverensi in allodio et in civitate Erfordiensi seu recepta sibi et ecclesie Moguntine, ac antiqua ecclesie Moguntine debent restituere domino et ecclesie sue predicte. Item sciatis quod civitas predicta obsessa fuit per amicos domini Treverensis, sed personaliter non fnit ibi, et per marchionem ultra quindene spacium. Marchio iacuit cum exercitu suo in claustro Montis sancti Cyriaci et amici domini ante dictum claustrum. Domini de- canus Moguntinus Hennannus de Lysberg et Ber. de Rosenberg vicedominus Aschaffen- burgensis fuerunt ibi pro domino. Dominus Fredericus de Wanh. fuit superior capitaneus domini Trevirensis, qui sustinuit pro domino et ecclesia Moguntina multum dampnum et labores, cui datur laus et honor pre oinnibus istorum duorum exercituum, quia quasi con- tinue bellavit cum Erfordiensibus una cum amicis domini. Item omnes viftes] Erford. sunt omnino combuste et desolate usque ad fundum. Item Erfordienses nemineni habuerunt pro adiutore nisi comitem de Kevernberg et dominum de Blankenli., quorum ville eciam sunt omnes combuste. Item dampna et expense etc. huius guerre estimantur ultra centum milia marcaruni argenti, quod a magistro Eck. de Saltza eorum notario audivi. Her. frater 736 REICHSSACHEN. (1336) SEPT. 23. vester semper fuit cum amicis domini et specialiter cum Ger. marschalco domini in exercitu. Item Ger. marschalcus dédit mihi nomine vestro viii. sol. gr. feria quarta ante Mathei, quos vobis reservam vel domino meo Dytm. presentabo, si vos michi demandetis. — Item de imperatore et. . rege Boem. nichil certi possum vobis scribere, nisi quod imperator intravit Austriam cum exercitu suo recedendo de campo, et dominus rex Boem. remansit in campo ; usque ad terciam diem exspectavit imperatorem, qui non rediit. Tune dominus rex intravit Boemiam cum exercitu suo. Et sic adhuc sunt ambo in partibus istis, ita quod nulla certa nova de ipsis habentur. — Item comes Gelrie noviter intravit terram Frysie cum exercitu suo, et bellavit cum Frisonibus, et obtinuit bellum, et interfecte* fuerunt ultra xvi.c. Frysones. — Item dominus Coloniensis intravit eciam noviter Marchiam cum magno exercitu et edificavit ibidem unam municionem contra comitem Marchie. — Item sciatis, quod heu Peter Gil est interfectus ab uno peásimo garcione infra quindenam, de quo do minus С. W. máximo tristatur. Item Muskinus mortuus est ante tres septimanas. — Item sciatis pro novis, quod rustici in Frankonia et circa Bischovesheim fecerimt unuiii regem nomine Armleder, qui cum magna potencia rusticorum pedibus, modici equis, vaduut ad opida et civitates et interfecerunt omnes lúdeos. Primo interfecerunt omnes lúdeos in Kitzingen, in Ossenfort, in Owe, in Mergentheim et adhuc bene in quatuor oppidis, quorum ' nomina nescio. Et eciam fuerunt ante civitatem Herbipolim, sed nichil profecerunt ibidem. Item fuerunt bene tribus vieibus ante Bischovesheim, quod nichil potuerunt ibidem faceré pre domini, qui semper fuerunt premuniti ad bellandum cum eis. Item interf[ecti] ludei sunt circa numerum xv.c, ut dicitur pro certo. Et adhuc dictus rex Armleder timetur a domino Treverensi, comitibus et nobilibus ac civitatibus neenon ludeis, qui cottidie pre- munient* se pre ipso et exercitu suo, timentes ipsum cum exercitu suo venire supra Renuin, quod dictus rex intendit faceré, si non caveatur. — Item sciatis, quod dominus contulit capellam in Konthechere Eberharde socio nostra. Item sciatis, quod heu Pingwia est circa mediam partem conbusta et curia episcopi totaliter cum omnibus [rebus], nichil deportando nisi litteras,, vinum, blada, equos, totum combussit in curia usque ad fundum. Item do- minus reemit castrum Wolvestein erga comitem Veldentzem, cui obligatum fuit feria tercia ante Mathei, et dedit sibi in prompta pecunia statim iiiun. cum c. libris ... in Treveri, quia dictus comes noluit unam horam carere de pecunia sua, ñeque exspectare. — Pater et domine mi, sitis niemor [mei], si unquam graciam possetis obtinere super ecclesia sancti Severi, quia libentius essem ibi quam alibi propter notitiam et pro .... si non ibi, tunc sit alibi, ubicunque vobis videbitur expediré. Commendo me vobis. Omnipotens deus, beata virgo et omnes sancti custodiant animam, corpus et res vestías ab omni malo. Amen. Scriptum per me Nycolaum, vestrum humilem servitorem, feria secunda post Mathei ewangeliste post mediam noctem quasi semi cecus. Rogo vos, ut [non] deridetis me, si in aliquo erravi, quia nimis festinavi et in tantum, quod non potui perlegere. Dominus meus vobis. Amen. Domino suo gracioso domino et magistro Rudolfo notario domini Trevirensis dandum. Aug dem orig. im conceptbuche des Rudolf Losse im archive ru Darmstadt. — 1 Hs. Ir mit abkilrzungsstrich.
entries.english:
Nicolaus writes to Rudolf Losse, envoy of Archbishop Baldwin of Trier at the papal court, about the archbishop's conflict with Erfurt, the war between Emperor Ludwig and King John of Bohemia, the persecution of the Jews, and other events. (Trier, 23 September 1336.)

Most gracious father and lord, I thank you for the many favors you have bestowed on me and, as I hope without doubt, will continue to bestow. Know that I immediately arranged for your letters to your brother Hermann of Pordicz and another man, which you sent through Wigand, the messenger of the lord of Trier, to be forwarded to Ysen, as I recently wrote to you. I believe that you have received an answer concerning those letters, since my lord and I recently sent you three letters from the aforesaid Hermann, your brother, and others. Your letter to the pastor of Bacherach, sent through you, is today being carried to him by Master Wicker, who is going above the Rhine. Your satchel has been kept for you by Ludwig, my lord's cellarer. I shall also keep the plants and the fire-steel for you, as I recently wrote. A cleric presented me with a package; I opened it and found one written book, two blank paper books, and a belt, just as you described in your letter, and I am keeping all of it for you. The same cleric also presented me with two books that day; on the following day I immediately sent them to your brother at Ysen with John, the schoolmaster, and Master Eck, notary of the citizens of Erfurt. I ask and advise you to arrange and procure various goods at court, because they can be found there at a better market than elsewhere, and send me whatever you wish me to keep for you. Do not send a messenger from court away empty-handed unless you give him something of your goods to carry. I have sent you letters three times, but I do not know whether they have been delivered, since you write nothing to me about them.

The old margravine arranged and concluded a settlement between the lord of Trier, the margrave of Meissen, and the people of Erfurt. The people of Erfurt are to pay the lord of Trier and the margrave a total of 10,000 marks of silver for all expenses, damages, and the settlement, in addition to the damage they caused the lord of Trier in his allod and in the city of Erfurt, or property taken from him and from the church of Mainz, which they must restore to the lord and to his aforesaid church. Know also that the aforesaid city was besieged by the friends of the lord of Trier, although he was not personally there, and by the margrave for more than a fortnight. The margrave lay with his army in the monastery of Mount Saint Cyriacus, while the lord's friends were in front of that monastery. The lord's dean of Mainz, Hermann von Lißberg, and Berthold von Rosenberg, vice-dom of Aschaffenburg, were there on the lord's behalf. Lord Friedrich of Wanh. was the supreme captain of the lord of Trier; he endured much damage and hardship for the lord and the church of Mainz, and he is given praise and honor above all those of the two armies, because he fought almost continuously with the people of Erfurt together with the lord's friends. All the villages of Erfurt were completely burned and laid waste to their foundations. The people of Erfurt had no helper except the count of Kevernberg and the lord of Blankenheim, whose villages too were all burned. The damages and expenses of this war are estimated at more than 100,000 marks of silver; I heard this from Master Eck of Saltza, their notary. Your brother Hermann was always with the lord's friends, especially with the lord's marshal Gerhard, in the army. Marshal Gerhard gave me, in your name, eight groschen on the Wednesday before Saint Matthew's day; I shall keep them for you or present them to my lord Dietmar if you ask me to.

Concerning the emperor and the king of Bohemia I can write nothing certain, except that the emperor entered Austria with his army while withdrawing from the field, and the lord king of Bohemia remained on the field. He waited for the emperor until the third day, but the emperor did not return. Then the lord king entered Bohemia with his army. Thus both are still in those regions, and no certain news about them is available. The count of Guelders recently entered Friesland with his army, fought the Frisians, and won the battle; more than 1,600 Frisians were killed. The lord of Cologne also recently entered the Mark with a large army and built a fortification there against the count of the Mark.

Know also, sadly, that Peter Gil was killed within a fortnight by a most wicked young man, at which Lord C. W. is deeply grieved. Muskinus died three weeks ago. As news, know that the peasants in Franconia and around Bischofsheim made a man named Armleder their king. With a great force of peasants on foot and a few on horseback, he went to towns and cities and killed all the Jews. First they killed all the Jews in Kitzingen, Ochsenfurt, Aub, and Mergentheim, and in about four other towns whose names I do not know. They also appeared before the city of Würzburg, but accomplished nothing there. They came before Bischofsheim about three times, but could do nothing there because the lord's men were always prepared to fight them. The Jews who were killed numbered about 1,500, as is said for certain. The aforesaid King Armleder is still feared by the lord of Trier, counts and nobles, cities, and also the Jews, who prepare themselves daily against him and his army, fearing that he will come with his army to the Rhine, which the said king intends to do if no precautions are taken.

Know also that the lord conferred the chapel at Konthechere on Eberhard, our associate. Sadly, about half of Pingwia has been burned, and the bishop's court was completely burned with all its goods; nothing was carried away except letters, wine, grain, and horses, and everything in the court was burned to the ground. The lord redeemed Wolvestein Castle from the count of Veldenz, to whom it had been pledged on the Tuesday before Saint Matthew's day, and immediately paid him in ready money 3,000 [units] with 100 pounds ... in Trier, because the count did not want to be without his money for a single hour or wait.

Most gracious father and lord, remember me if you should ever be able to obtain a favor concerning the church of Saint Severus, for I would rather be there than anywhere else because of my acquaintance and for [the unfinished purpose in the source]. If not there, then let it be elsewhere, wherever you think best. I commend myself to you. May almighty God, the blessed Virgin, and all the saints protect your soul, body, and possessions from every evil. Amen. Written by me, Nicolaus, your humble servant, on the Monday after the feast of Matthew the Evangelist, after midnight, almost half-blind. Please do not laugh at me if I have made any mistake, for I wrote in great haste and to such an extent that I could not reread it. My lord be with you. Amen. To be delivered to his gracious lord and master Rudolf, notary of the lord of Trier. From the original in Rudolf Losse's draft book in the archive at Darmstadt. [Editorial note: the manuscript has an abbreviation mark over the numeral.]
